The dropped-paren rows of the re-emission work queue (issue
01a167da-3323), reduced and held to perl 5.44.0.

op/lexsub.t:350 was the queue's one dropped-paren row: `state sub END
{ shift }` declares a lexical END, and `END('jkqeudth')` calls it. psc read
the word as the END phaser, so the call's `(` came back as a `;`. No op
carries P on the call: its parens are a call's. toke.c looks a word up in
the pad before its keyword table, so a lexical sub shadows every statement
keyword parseTheRest reads; `CORE::END` still names the phaser, and the
lexical's scope ends with its block.

Then the three logical assignments 01a16602-5f1a's review found unmapped in
the OPf_PARENS op table, and issue 3323's original defect, `\(my @a)`,
which 01a16602-75d4 fixed.

=== the op/lexsub.t row: a lexical END called in an eval block
use feature 'state';
sub is { 1 }
{
  state sub END { shift }
  is eval{END('jkqeudth')}, 'jkqeudth',
    'state sub END {shift} implies @_, not @ARGV';
}
--- facts
faithful
# i  <1> entersub lKS ->7 over h  <0> padcv[&END:7,10] s: no P on the call

=== a lexical BEGIN called at statement start
my sub BEGIN { 1 }
BEGIN('x');
--- facts
faithful

=== a lexical require called at statement start
my sub require { 1 }
require('x');
--- facts
faithful

=== a lexical use called at statement start
my sub use { 1 }
use('x');
--- facts
faithful

=== a lexical class called at statement start
my sub class { 1 }
class('x');
--- facts
faithful

=== a lexical END's scope ends with its block
{ my sub END { 1 } }
END { 2 }
--- facts
faithful
# perl -e '{ my sub BEGIN {} } BEGIN { print "phaser\n" }' prints phaser

=== CORE::END is the phaser under a lexical END
my sub END { 1 }
CORE::END { 2 }
--- facts
faithful

=== a parenthesised ||=
our $x;
my $v = ($x ||= 1);
--- facts
faithful
# -        <1> null sKP/1 ->7, over orassign

our $x;
my $v = ($x //= 1);
--- facts
faithful
# -        <1> null sKP/1 ->7, over dorassign

=== a parenthesised &&=
our $x;
my $v = ($x &&= 1);
--- facts
faithful
# -        <1> null sKP/1 ->7, over andassign
